primitives.name: Explainable ML Model Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question Which explainable supervised ML model best forecasts a professional footballer's development one year ahead — both in player quality (SciSkill rating) and monetary transfer value (Estimated Transfer Value, ETV) — when judged on predictive accuracy AND explainability AND uncertainty quantification, as a practitioner (club) would require?
primitives.assumptions: Model performance evaluated on accuracy, explainability, and UQ metrics; practitioners prioritize these three.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Models must be interpretable and support uncertainty estimation.

This is achieved through a structured pipeline involving feature engineering, model selection, and uncertainty quantification. The primary model identified is Random Forest (RF), which offers a balance between accuracy, interpretability, and built-in uncertainty quantification via bagging. The framework is adaptable to other domains such as NFL, where similar forecasting tasks arise. The framework's robustness hinges on proper feature selection and handling of temporal dependencies. The paper acknowledges limitations including proprietary data constraints and lack of statistical significance testing for model comparisons. The dual nature of the forecasting task—quality and value—requires distinct but complementary feature sets and model configurations.
